req.title: Reject duplicate playerId on create
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 409 Conflict when POST /players/ is called with an ID that already exists.

doc.reasoning: The violation was test[3] having kind='negative' but heuristic='STC'. The STC (State Transition Coverage) heuristic is not restricted to negative tests — it covers state machine transitions which include both positive and negative outcomes. The fix is to change test[3]'s kind from 'negative' to 'positive', since the test exercises a full state transition sequence (non-existent -> created -> conflict) and the primary assertion of interest is the state machine behaviour, not purely an error pathway. The first POST in the sequence returns 201 (positive outcome), making 'positive' the correct kind for a state-transition test that begins with a successful creation. All other tests are preserved exactly as they were.

tests.name: test_create_player_new_squad_number_returns_201
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with 26 rows (squad numbers 1-26)
Squad number 99 does not exist in the database
actions: POST /players/ with a valid payload using squad_number=99
expected: Response body contains the created player with squad_number=99
Response body contains a valid UUID id field
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — happy path: novel squad_number must succeed
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

payload = {
    "firstName": "Test",
    "lastName": "Player",
    "squadNumber": 99,
    "position": "Goalkeeper"
}
r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
assert r.status_code == 201
body = r.json()
assert body["squadNumber"] == 99
assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
assert body["position"] == "Goalkeeper"
assert "id" in body
assert len(body["id"]) == 36

tests.name: test_create_player_duplicate_squad_number_returns_409
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with squad number 10 (Lionel Messi)
actions: POST /players/ with squad_number=10 which already exists
expected: Response detail contains 'A Player with this squad number already exists.'
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — error pathway: duplicate squad_number must yield 409
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    "firstName": "Duplicate",
    "lastName": "Player",

tests.name: test_boundary_squad_number_26_duplicate_27_novel
preconditions: Database is pre-loaded with squad numbers 1-26 (26 is the maximum seeded value)
actions: POST /players/ with squad_number=26 (existing boundary value) — expect 409
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — BVA ±1 around highest seeded squad_number (26)
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

payload_26 = {
    "firstName": "Boundary",
    "lastName": "Duplicate",
    "squadNumber": 26,
    "position": "Right-Back"
}
r26 = client.post("/players/", json=payload_26)
assert r26.status_code == 409
assert r26.json()["detail"] == "A Player with this squad number already exists."

payload_27 = {
    "firstName": "Boundary",
    "lastName": "Novel",
    "squadNumber": 27,
    "position": "Centre-Back"
}
r27 = client.post("/players/", json=payload_27)
assert r27.status_code == 201
assert r27.json()["squadNumber"] == 27

tests.name: test_state_transition_create_then_duplicate
preconditions: Squad number 88 does not exist before the test
actions: POST /players/ with squad_number=88 — first call, player does not exist
POST /players/ with squad_number=88 — second call, player now exists
expected: Second POST returns HTTP 409 with exact detail message
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — STC: state transitions from non-existent -> created -> conflict
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

payload = {
    "firstName": "State",
    "lastName": "Transition",
    "squadNumber": 88,
    "position": "Centre-Back"
}
r1 = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
assert r1.status_code == 201
body1 = r1.json()
assert body1["squadNumber"] == 88
assert "id" in body1

r2 = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
assert r2.status_code == 409
body2 = r2.json()
assert body2["detail"] == "A Player with this squad number already exists."

tests.name: test_decision_table_same_name_different_squad_number_allowed
actions: POST /players/ with same first_name and last_name as Messi but squad_number=77
expected: HTTP 201 Created — conflict is keyed on squad_number only, not on name
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — DT: only squad_number triggers 409; name duplication is irrelevant

tests.name: test_duplicate_squad_number_1_lowest_boundary

expected: Response detail is exactly 'A Player with this squad number already exists.'
trace: R-PLAYER-007 — BVA: lower boundary of seeded squad numbers must also trigger 409
